newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU ministers to meet new Congo's Kabila next week. [CORRECTED 17:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: EU ministers to meet new Congo's Kabila next week. [CORRECTED 17:25 GMT]

text.p: Three European Union ministers will visit the Democratic Republic of the Congo, formerly Zaire, next week to talk with President Laurent Kabila about the country's move to democracy and future relations with the EU.

Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo, his Luxembourg counterpart Jacques Poos and British Foreign Office minister of state Tony Lloyd will spend Monday and Tuesday in the capital Kinshasa, the EU presidency said in a statement on Friday.
The ministers, who represent the so-called troika of the past, present and future six-month EU presidencies, will also meet Kabila's Foreign Minister Bizima Karaha.

"They will speak with (them) about the process of democratisation in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the humanitarian assistance that the EU could offer this country, and its future relations with the EU," the statement said.

The visit was planned at a Luxembourg meeting of EU foreign ministers in June at which they expressed concern over reports of human rights abuses in former Zaire and said the bloc would keep close tabs on its progress towards democracy.
Kabila seized office in May after ousting ailing president Mobutu Sese Seko following a seven month civil war. (Corrects from 17-month civil war).
